subject: humanities
notes: The Lahore Fort, in Pakistan, contains a wall known as the Picture Wall.
The wall stretches for about 450 meters along the fort's northern and western sides.
It was begun under the Mughal emperor Jahangir and completed in 1632, during the reign of Shah Jahan.
It is decorated with tile mosaics showing elephant fights, polo matches, angels, and other scenes.
It is considered one of the largest murals in the world.
Conservation work begun in the 2010s has restored parts of the wall.
stem: The student wants to emphasize both the size of the Picture Wall and the variety of its subjects. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Stretching about 450 meters, the Picture Wall depicts subjects ranging from elephant fights and polo matches to angels.
choices.B: Considered one of the largest murals in the world, the Picture Wall of the Lahore Fort stretches for about 450 meters.
choices.C: The Picture Wall in Pakistan's Lahore Fort is decorated with tile mosaics showing elephant fights, polo matches, and angels.
choices.D: Begun under Jahangir and completed in 1632 under Shah Jahan, the Picture Wall of the Lahore Fort has recently been partly restored.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: the wall's size and the variety of what it shows. The notes give the size (about 450 meters) and a range of subjects (elephant fights, polo matches, angels). Only one choice includes both.
explanation.A: Correct. It gives the wall's length and a range of very different subjects.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It stresses the wall's size twice over but says nothing about its subjects. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It shows the variety of subjects but leaves out the wall's size.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It gives the wall's history and conservation, not its size or subjects.
